previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a man with a history of heavy alcohol use, COPD, and chronic pain from prior injuries, was admitted after being found unresponsive on a sofa. He presented with pneumonia, alcohol and benzodiazepine intoxication, and hypoxia. He received initial treatment with levofloxacin and flagyl in the ED, but due to prior resistance, was switched to Bactrim. He refused further testing, including a CT for possible pulmonary embolism, and declined breathing treatments, nicotine replacement, and social work support. He was treated for alcohol withdrawal with diazepam and showed some improvement in oxygen levels. Despite medical advice, he chose to leave the hospital against medical advice on the second day of admission, after receiving only two days of appropriate antibiotic therapy.
problems: Acute alcoholic intoxication in alcoholism, continuous

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M with HTN, COPD, alcohol abuse, and recent PNAs 
presenting with intoxication and hypoxia.  

# Hypoxia- Most likely related to undertreated pneumonia and 
possible recurrent aspiration events while intoxicated. The 
patient was initially on 2L of O2 with sats in the mid ___, and 
was able to be weaned down.  He was started on Bactrim to 
continue the course he did not complete for PNA with sputum cx 
showing coag+ staph sensitive to Bactrim, as well as Flagyl 
given concern for aspiration.  Flagyl was discontinued during 
admission given low concern for aspiration and clinical 
improvement.  There was concern for COPD exacerbation given his 
smoking history and concern for poor air movement on lung exam, 
however he refused to take nebulizer treatments.  He improved 
clinically and was discharged with sats around 94% on room air 
and will complete a total 7 day course of Bactrim to end on 
___.

# Alcohol abuse- Patient has had many admission recently, and 
has been intoxicated during all. Last drink was at 4 AM on 
___, patient was treated for alcohol withdrawal with 
diazepam every 2 hours as needed for CIWA >10.  The patient 
asked for higher doses of diazepam and was given 15 mg every 2 
hours.  On discharge his symptoms of withdrawal were improved, 
but he received 90 mg of diazepam on day prior to discharge and 
will likely need a benzodiazepine taper on admission to an 
alcohol treatment facility.  The patient was resistant to 
decreases in dose and frequency of diazepam while in house.

The possiblity of section 35 was considered in the past and 
during this admission it was completed by social work and 
approved by the legal department.  The patient was noted to be 
medically stable for discharge on ___ and the legal 
department was contacted.  Patient was discharged in police 
custody for possible admission to an alcohol treatment center, 
given his frequent admissions for alcohol abuse. Folate, 
multivitamin and thiamine were started during admission and 
should be continued after discharge.

# HTN: pt had been on enalapril and metoprolol at home, which he 
had stopped taking.  These medications were restarted during 
admission, and HCTZ was continued.

compliance with treatment.  Evaluate for progression.

FINDINGS:

AP and lateral views of the chest are compared to previous exams from ___.  Linear opacities identified at the lung bases, most suggestive
of atelectasis given their configuration.  There is also subtle residual
retrocardiac opacity which has improved since ___.  Elsewhere, the
lungs are clear.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal.  Osseous and soft
tissue structures are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Subtle residual retrocardiac opacity, which has improved since exam from
___, which could represent resolving infection; however, repeat
examination is recommended in four to six weeks to document complete
resolution of this finding.  Bibasilar atelectasis.
